sessions.phase_label: Report requirements, format discussion, and project setup
Initial design concept and visual refinements

requirements.title: Premium Report Visual Style
requirements.definition: The report must have a polished, readable, consistent commercial design suitable for a paid vehicle-security assessment.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers only the holistic visual quality and consistency of the report; specific dashboard, header, footer, warning, and content-structure behaviors remain separate Requirements.

requirements.title: Front-Page Result Dashboard
requirements.definition: The front page must prominently communicate the vehicle security score and associated risk outcome as the report's primary result.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers prominence and presentation of the primary score and risk result; the detailed explanation of causes and weaknesses is independently scannable and remains separate.

requirements.title: Scannable Front-Page Result Explanation
requirements.definition: The front page must concisely explain the main reason for the rating and the primary security weaknesses in an easy-to-scan form.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the concise cause-and-weakness summary rather than score prominence or longer explanatory copy elsewhere in the report.

requirements.title: Transparent Scoring Summary
requirements.definition: The report must present a clear scoring table with categories, maximum scores, customer scores, and the total score.
requirements.boundary_note: The table columns and totals are attributes of one scoring-summary mechanism rather than separate Requirements.

requirements.title: Prioritized Security Upgrade Path
requirements.definition: Security recommendations must be presented as a practical, action-led upgrade path ordered by priority.
requirements.boundary_note: Immediate actions, priority upgrades, and secondary upgrades are priority levels within one recommendation mechanism.

requirements.title: Consistent Internal-Page Header
requirements.definition: Pages after the front page must use a subtle, consistent header containing appropriate report-identification and confidentiality information.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers header presence and presentation; correctness of the RR version code shown in the header belongs to the report-identifier consistency Requirement.

requirements.title: Consistent Report Footer
requirements.definition: Every report page, including the final page, must retain a clean and consistent footer.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers footer presence and visual consistency across pages; version-code correctness within the footer is tracked separately.

requirements.title: Refined Confidentiality Distribution Warning
requirements.definition: The final-page distribution warning must remain clear while being visually restrained enough not to overpower the page or interfere with its footer.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the warning block's clarity and visual dominance; restoration and consistency of the page footer remain a separate Requirement.

requirements.title: Four Coordinated Report Variants
requirements.definition: The deliverable must contain coordinated RR01, RR02, RR03, and RR04 report variants using the same overall design and selected according to customer risk level.
requirements.boundary_note: The four reports form one coordinated variant set; their exposure-band mapping, identifiers, and risk-specific wording are independently testable and remain separate Requirements.

requirements.title: Correct Exposure Band Mapping
requirements.definition: Each report variant must display its correct exposure category: RR01 Severe, RR02 Elevated, RR03 Reduced, and RR04 Lower Exposure.
requirements.boundary_note: The four report-to-band assignments are values of one classification mapping; report codes and profile-specific prose are separate behaviors.

requirements.title: Version-Specific Report Identifier Consistency
requirements.definition: Each report must consistently display its own RR identifier in front-page details, internal headers, and footers.
requirements.boundary_note: The display locations are coupled by one version-identifier consistency rule; header and footer visual presence are evaluated separately.

requirements.title: Risk-Profile-Appropriate Report Wording
requirements.definition: Narrative wording in each report variant must accurately reflect that variant's exposure profile rather than reusing severe-exposure language indiscriminately.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers semantic alignment of prose with the report's risk profile; ordinary typographical and sentence corrections are separate.

requirements.title: Accurate Final Report Copy
requirements.definition: Specified report text must be free of identified typographical errors and must use the client-approved replacement sentences.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers concrete copy corrections such as the driveway typo and revised assessment note; risk-band-specific narrative consistency remains separate.

requirements.title: Editable Customer-Specific Fields
requirements.definition: The report templates must allow customer-specific values such as vehicle details, dates, report IDs, scores, weaknesses, recommendations, and notes to be updated cleanly.
requirements.boundary_note: The individual editable fields are parameters of one template-editability mechanism; file-format delivery and final PDF exports are separate Requirements.

requirements.title: Editable Source Templates in Required Formats
requirements.definition: Editable source templates must be delivered for all four report variants in the client-confirmed formats, including Canva, so future customer reports can be edited and exported.
requirements.boundary_note: Required file formats and four-version coverage are attributes of the source-template handoff; customer-field behavior, PDF exports, and supporting design assets remain separate.

requirements.title: Final PDF Exports
requirements.definition: Customer-ready final PDF exports must be provided for RR01, RR02, RR03, and RR04.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers delivery of final exported PDFs, not the editable templates' capability to generate future PDFs.

requirements.title: Reusable Design Asset Package
requirements.definition: The handoff must include the fonts, icons, logos, colour codes, and other design assets needed to edit and export future reports.
requirements.boundary_note: Fonts, icons, logos, and colour codes are components of one reusable asset package rather than separate Requirements.

unresolved_candidates.description: The client refers to minor changes contained only in an attached image; the unavailable attachment prevents safe routing to specific Requirements.
